recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-22635 unless a future work-group decision changes the isModifier examples.
issue_request: FHIR-22635 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request for FHIR-core-conformance-rules asking that the isModifier examples explicitly say whether Observation.status and Observation.subject are modifier elements. The accepted resolution said to note Observation.status is a modifier and Observation.subject is not.
initial_application: Commit a9713d220c784b78b225c88f407e2f5706524567, "Apply FHIR-22635 to clarify Is-Modifier examples", changed source/conformance-rules.html to prepend "Observation.status is a modifier" and "Observation.subject is not a modifier" to the respective examples. Current blame confirms those classifications remain from that commit.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists conformance-rules.html as the Conformance page, and source/documentation.html plus source/conformance-module.html link to it, so source/conformance-rules.html is in current build scope. Current source also states Observation.code is not a modifier. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no directly relevant later decision or community discussion that conflicts with the applied wording; broad Jira search also returned FHIR-16136 about Observation.focus, but that concerns a different Observation element.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/conformance-rules.html already explicitly classifies Observation.status as a modifier and Observation.subject as not a modifier.
